_comment: An example manifest, with example data. Copy it to layers.json, point `sources` at your own
paths, and replace the layers with yours. Everything under rstack/example/ is invented.
Read `rules` top to bottom like a routing table: the FIRST rule that matches an item wins, so
the specific rule goes above the general one. Every rule needs a `layer` that exists and
either a `match` glob with 3+ literal characters or `any_of` keywords of 4+ characters;
coverage.py rejects a catch-all, FAILS a rule that matches nothing, and FAILS an `enforcer`
path that does not exist. An item no rule claims FAILS until you give it a rule, or an
exclusion with a written reason. 'Not ours' is a reason. 'Misc' is not.
Run `coverage.py --config rstack/layers.example.json` as shipped and it FAILS on purpose:
stale-guard.py is unmapped. That is the tool working.

01-orchestration.title: Orchestration
01-orchestration.playbook: One conductor, many workers. Workers reach the conductor through a script, never by messaging it directly, so a wake is a decision someone made deliberately.

02-guards.title: Guards
02-guards.playbook: A guard refuses rather than crashes. Most hook systems block only on a specific exit code or decision, so a guard that raises is not a weaker guard, it is no guard, and it fails silently. Add a guard with its test in the same change.

03-comms.title: Outbound communication
03-comms.playbook: Anything that leaves gets linted before it leaves and approved as the exact bytes that will be sent. The thing that sends is not the thing that approves.

04-work.title: The actual work
04-work.playbook: The reason the rest exists. Frozen tests, a baseline you can run, a yield check that fails a line of work spending without finding anything. Every claim says whether it found something new.

05-publishing.title: Publishing and egress
05-publishing.playbook: Nothing leaves without a scan for private material, and an agent whose output leaves runs with an empty identity so personal context cannot leak into it.

06-memory.title: Memory and the knowledge base
06-memory.playbook: The main checkout is never edited by a session: work in a worktree and land. One fact per file, with an index.

07-jobs.title: Scheduled and background jobs
07-jobs.playbook: Wait on an event, do not poll. Heavy compute goes somewhere else; the machine running the fleet is not the machine running the models.

08-mods.title: Session mechanics
08-mods.playbook: Context limits, handoffs and naming. A long session hands off through a written file rather than compacting silently.

exclusions.reason: a third-party updater installed with the vendor's own tooling; not ours to map or change
